transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aperture Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Infra), Sara Thompson (Product)

---
Summary: Quick kickoff to align on harness integration for benchmark runs. Client wants to validate production scripts against Redwood's streaming and non-streaming paths and agree acceptance criteria.

---
00:00:05 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we ran a quick agenda slide but i'll just call it out, scope, success criteria, scripts, streaming vs non-streaming, timeline. Samir's gonna drive the technical bits.
00:00:23 Priya Nair: Hi, thanks. We're excited. we mostly want to know how our current inference scripts behave on Redwood versus our in-house stack, especially tail latency under mixed conversational loads.
00:00:35 Samir Gupta: great, thanks. can you confirm the script types? you mentioned a 1:1 chat bot and a batch embedding pipeline earlier?
00:00:46 Priya Nair: yes two primary flows — interactive support chat (short to medium tokens, often streaming used by our UI) and nightly batch rerank/embedding (longer, non-streaming). plus a low-volume longform generation used by content team.
00:01:05 Marcus Lee: and we have a proxy layer that injects auth headers; for the POC we'd prefer not to rework the entire stack. we can hand you scripts plus a replay harness.
00:01:17 Lena Ortiz: perfect that's the ideal. Samir, can you outline the harness adapter approach?
00:01:23 Samir Gupta: sure, so typically we create a small adapter that maps customer request schema to the Redwood client. for streaming, the harness needs to handle chunked responses and reassemble. for non-streaming it's straightforward. the gotchas are: kv cache warmup, prompt prefixes, and any stateful session handling.
00:01:47 Priya Nair: when you say kv cache warmup is that going to change p95? we see big improvement if cache is warmed. we want both cold-start and steady-state numbers.
00:01:58 Samir Gupta: exactly. we'll run a cold-start sweep (first N sessions on cold nodes) then a warm run after steady traffic to capture both tails. we recommend at least 30 minutes of sustained traffic for steady numbers based on your RPS.
00:02:16 Sara Thompson: quick question — for our UI streaming path, we care about p50 and p95 for first-token latency and end-to-end render. does Redwood report token-level breakdowns?
00:02:27 Samir Gupta: yes we provide token-level latencies and per-request breakdown. the console also shows cost-per-token and per-route aggregates. small note, streaming path may appear slightly higher on per-token overhead but lowers perceived latency since first tokens arrive sooner.
00:02:46 Lena Ortiz: ok let's ground acceptance criteria. Priya, what are your internal targets?
00:02:53 Priya Nair: for interactive chat — p50 first-token < 120ms, p95 first-token < 450ms, end-to-end for 200 token responses < 1.2s ideally. For batch embedding: throughput >= 20k embeddings/hour with 95% success and cost per embedding within 15% of our in-house numbers. For correctness, we'd run sample evals and expect delta < 3% on rubric metrics.
00:03:21 Samir Gupta: those are aggressive but plausible — depends on model variant and deployment (hosted vs dedicated). we can propose two POC tracks: hosted (quick, lower cost) and dedicated reserved GPU for higher consistent throughput.
00:03:37 Marcus Lee: we prefer dedicated for SLA reasons if perf matches; but during the trial hosted capability is fine to validate functional correctness. also we need to vet encryption/KMS and audit logs before any data ingress.
00:03:51 Lena Ortiz: noted. security will be part of the checklist. we'll share SOC2 and our audit log docs. Samir, what's the minimal harness work to run their scripts?
00:04:04 Samir Gupta: minimal is ~3 parts: 1) a mapping layer that converts their request format to Redwood SDK calls; 2) a runner that replays traffic with adjustable RPS and concurrency; 3) a collector that captures latencies, token counts, errors, and optionally token-level traces. for streaming we need to wire up server-sent events or websocket stubs depending on how their UI expects chunks.
00:04:29 Priya Nair: our streaming client uses websockets. can you support that?
00:04:33 Samir Gupta: we can emulate websocket clients in the harness — Samir: (laughs) i've done it before. small caveat: replay fidelity — if your UI logic cancels streams mid-response, we should capture that behavior in scripts.
00:04:50 Sara Thompson: yes we do terminate some streams on user nav. we'll include those cases.
00:04:55 Marcus Lee: network: for dedicated tests we'll need to allowlist Redwood test IPs in our staging VPC. timeline for that?
00:05:04 Lena Ortiz: we'll provide allowlist IPs once we lock the test window; i'd aim for the week of 2026-12-07 for dedicated runs if that works.
00:05:12 Priya Nair: that could work but we need results earlier for an internal review on 2026-12-14. so earlier is better.
00:05:20 Samir Gupta: note, initial adapter + small smoke run we can do in 3 business days after scripts are uploaded. large acceptance runs will take longer since we need to coordinate warmup and sustained traffic windows.
00:05:33 Lena Ortiz: good, so next steps rough: Priya uploads scripts by 12/01, Samir runs adapter smoke by 12/04, Lena shares POC scope/pricing by 12/02, and then we aim for dedicated window 12/07-12/09.
00:05:47 Priya Nair: sounds good. i want to dig into the benchmark specifics — what configs will you vary? batch size, quantization, streaming chunk size?
00:05:58 Samir Gupta: yes those plus model variant, sequence length, and KV cache policies. we'll catalog knobs: 1) quantization (fp16/int8), 2) batching windows, 3) streaming chunk sizes and flush intervals, 4) model variant (llamaX-small/medium/large or open weights), 5) placement (hosted/dedicated). we'll include a matrix runs and prioritize per your success metrics.
00:06:23 Marcus Lee: how do you measure cost parity? our accounting prefers cost per 1k tokens and amortized infra cost during test. can Redwood provide a cost model?
00:06:33 Samir Gupta: yes we export token counts and compute time, and we can map to Redwood pricing or an estimated infra cost for dedicated. we'll produce cost-per-call and cost-per-1k-token numbers.
00:06:45 Sara Thompson: on correctness checks — we have an eval harness that scores outputs on intent and factuality. can you run our eval set as part of the acceptance?
00:06:55 Samir Gupta: absolutely, bring a small labeled eval set. for streaming vs non-streaming we should see identical outputs if model and prompt are same; differences usually come from decoding interruptions or timeout thresholds. we'll include a correctness delta check.
00:07:10 Priya Nair: okay what about telemetry? we need per-request ids to correlate with our logs. can the harness pass through our trace ids?
00:07:19 Samir Gupta: yes, the adapter can forward headers and we'll capture those as request tags in the telemetry. we'll include a sample mapping in the adapter readme.
00:07:29 Lena Ortiz: let's talk failure modes — what happens when stream fails mid-response? how will acceptance consider retries?
00:07:36 Samir Gupta: we'll capture failure rates and retry behavior. acceptance should include retry success within a single attempt window; repeated retry might mask poor latency. recommendation: limit retries for acceptance measurement and report raw failure-rate plus recovered success-rate.
00:07:54 Marcus Lee: about SOC2 and encryption — who owns keys in dedicated? we use our own KMS, not Redwood's.
00:07:59 Lena Ortiz: for private/dedicated deployments we support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own keys pattern; we'll have security go through details once the contract track starts. for hosted POC we can do ephemeral keys and ensure encryption in transit.
00:08:16 Priya Nair: ok good. small thing — our batch jobs sometimes hit long sequences up to 4k tokens. will that change perf dramatically?
00:08:26 Samir Gupta: yes, sequence length increases compute and memory. part of the benchmark matrix should include short, medium, long sequences — we'll profile memory and OOM risk, and recommend model/quantization accordingly.
00:08:37 Sara Thompson: for streaming case, do you measure first-byte latency separately from throughput?
00:08:44 Samir Gupta: yes, we'll report first-byte and steady-state throughput. sometimes batching has overhead for first byte, but gives better throughput; streaming favors lower first-byte latency.
00:08:56 Priya Nair: one more: our privacy team requires retention windows for logs. what's your default?
00:09:03 Lena Ortiz: we have configurable retention; for POC we can set short retention and disable storage of raw prompts if required. we'll share the retention controls doc.
00:09:13 Priya Nair: great.
00:09:16 Lena Ortiz: ok i want to capture concrete success criteria now so we all agree. repeating: interactive — p50 < 120ms first-token, p95 < 450ms first-token; end-to-end <1.2s for 200 tokens. batch — throughput >=20k embeddings/hour and cost within 15% of current. correctness delta <3%. are we aligned?
00:09:39 Priya Nair: aligned, though we may accept p95 < 600ms if dedicated options need time; but we'll aim for 450ms.
00:09:48 Marcus Lee: aligned. and security acceptance: must have audit logs and allowlist setup before production handoff.
00:09:56 Lena Ortiz: noted. timeline motions: scripts by 12/01, scope doc by 12/02, smoke runs by 12/04, dedicated window 12/07-12/09, final acceptance report by 12/14. does that sequence work for everyone?
00:10:10 Priya Nair: yes, provided the smoke runs show no major regressions.
00:10:15 Samir Gupta: i'll build the adapter to support websocket streaming and include a toggle to switch to chunked-server-sent-events in case their UI differs. i'll also include a small harness config to simulate user cancels.
00:10:28 Sara Thompson: awesome. any blockers on our side? we'll need to sanitize scripts for PII before upload.
00:10:34 Priya Nair: we'll sanitize and annotate which fields are placeholders.
00:10:38 Lena Ortiz: perfect. last bits — do we want a small demo of the harness running against a synthetic script next week?
00:10:45 Samir Gupta: yes we can demo a 10-minute run with synthetic traffic to show latency charts and token traces. propose 2026-12-03 16:00 UTC for the demo.
00:10:56 Priya Nair: that works for me. Marcus and Sara?
00:10:59 Marcus Lee: yes.
00:11:00 Sara Thompson: yes.
00:11:02 Lena Ortiz: great. I'll send calendar invites.
00:11:06 ---
00:11:06 Wrap and recap:
00:11:08 Lena Ortiz: recap: Priya provide scripts and traces by 2026-12-01 and sanitize; Lena share POC scope/pricing by 12/02; Samir deliver adapter smoke test by 12/04 and demo 12/03; dedicated runs targeted 12/07-12/09; final acceptance report by 12/14. security doc and IP allowlist to follow.
00:11:34 Priya Nair: thanks all, talk soon.
00:11:37 Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and filler words removed for readability; transcription may have small recognition errors for product names.
